lines.s: Processing
When the Threema Website is called up, information, including personal data, is automatically sent to the Threema Servers by the browser on the Visitor’s device, processed, and stored in a log file.

After processing the full IP address, normally only the first two digits of a Visitor’s IP address are stored in the log file, unless an error occurred when calling up the Threema Website. In case of an error, the full IP address is stored in the log file.

On pages of the Threema Website that contain forms, the respective form is loaded from the server of the marketing automation solution Aivie when the page is called up. In the process, the Visitor’s IP address as well as browser and device information are transmitted to Aivie (see Section 2.L. ).

To protect against overload attacks (so-called “DDoS attacks”), Threema uses the service of Myra Security GmbH, Landsberger Strasse 187, 80687 Munich, Germany (hereinafter “Myra”). Only during an attack is the data traffic to the Threema Servers rerouted via Myra’s filtering infrastructure (so-called “on-demand” operation), which is operated, as a rule, in Switzerland and, as part of its georedundant design, possibly also in Germany. There, malicious data traffic is filtered out and the remaining data traffic is forwarded to the Threema Servers. To the extent that personal data is processed in this context, this exclusively concerns IP addresses; the contents of the communication remain encrypted and cannot be viewed by Myra. Outside of an attack, data traffic is not routed via Myra.
